FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Check the speedometer frequently rather than relying on your sense of speed, especially after leaving a high-speed road for a slower local road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Obey posted speed-limit signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Anticipate stops early because abrupt braking can cause a skid and leaves following drivers less time to avoid a collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Looking far ahead allows gradual slowing or a safe lane change that may avoid a panic stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A02
For emergency or slippery-road braking with ABS, apply the brakes as firmly as possible and steer if needed to avoid a collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A02
For emergency or slippery-road braking without ABS, brake as firmly as possible while preventing wheel lock. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
Observe the road ahead, both sides and the area behind the vehicle, remaining alert for unexpected events. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Use headlights at night and whenever seeing becomes difficult. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
Avoid looking away from the road for more than a few seconds at once; pull safely off the road before consulting a map. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
Remain calm and do not take traffic problems personally when dealing with aggressive driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Avoid eye contact with aggressive drivers and do not challenge them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
Keep away from drivers behaving erratically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A03
Avoid phone or CB-radio conversations while moving; even hands-free conversation diverts attention from driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A03
Delaware prohibits driving with headphones or earphones covering or inserted into both ears. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A03
Do not slow merely to watch a crash, ticket or roadside event; keep watching the road and pass the activity as safely as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A03
Scanning ahead, to the sides and behind helps identify approaching hazards, road users and signs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A03
Look far enough ahead to prepare for slowing or changing lanes; the handbook recommends looking at least 10 seconds ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A03
A 10-second look-ahead means the distance the vehicle will cover during the next 10 seconds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A03
In city traffic, the handbook recommends trying to look at least one block ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A03
To measure look-ahead time, choose a stationary roadside object about as far ahead as you are watching. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A03
Count seconds until reaching that object; the count measures how many seconds ahead you were looking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0116]
